intent: The preview card, portalled and positioned beside its trigger, shown while its HoverCard is open.
typical_uses: A short summary of what the trigger links to, such as a name, an avatar and a line of detail

dont_use_when.situation: A one-line label for its trigger
A panel with fields or buttons the user has to operate

invariants.text: The card is in the DOM only while the hover card is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed card renders nothing.

Without `container`, the card portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the card only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.
The pointer can travel from the trigger onto the card without closing it, and the card stays open while the pointer rests on it.
The card renders no caret pointing at its trigger; there is no prop to add one.
The card fades, scales and slides on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` hover-card.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Fill the card with a long article or a form
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep it to a preview - hover-card.module.css fixes the card at 16rem wide, so longer content grows into a tall narrow column

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the card portals into; an explicit null renders no card until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between trigger and card, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the card is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, instant, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through hover-card.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside HoverCardContent; only its `container` is exposed, as HoverCardContent's own prop.
Composed inside HoverCardContent; its placement props are exposed on HoverCardContent itself.

good.title: A card placed to the right of its trigger
A card portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Content with no HoverCard root around it
bad.why: The primitive's Portal and Popup read the nearest HoverCard root's state through context and throw when there is none.
